content:
mike.s: FYI — customer (Acme Corp, ticket ACME-812) reporting constant parse failures when using strict structured output. They call with response_format=json&mode=strict and intermittently get "Invalid JSON" errors.

anna.d: Can you paste the exact request they send and a raw response example?

mike.s: Pasting the curl they used and the raw body we captured from our gateway logs:

mike.s: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "Accept: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"xlarge","input":"summarize: ...","response_format":"json","mode":"strict"}'
```

mike.s: Raw response body we logged (status 200 from our edge):

mike.s: ```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head><title>Login</title></head>
  <body>Redirecting to login...</body>
</html>
```

mike.s: Customer sees "Invalid JSON: unexpected token '<'" — they only hit it ~1-2% of requests.

cheng.w: That pattern looks like an auth redirect being injected somewhere (401 -> HTML login page). If strict structured mode is on we treat non-JSON responses as fatal parse failures.

lauren.k: Do we have any recent edge or proxy deploys that could cause Accept header or auth header to be dropped or rewritten?

mike.s: We traced a few samples: when it fails, our edge logs show a 302 to /sso/login from upstream with Content-Type: text/html. Upstream responded 302 because token validation service returned 401 and triggered SSO.

mike.s: Gateway snippet from logs: ```
REQUEST: POST /v1/generate
Headers: {Authorization: "Bearer sk_live_...", Accept: "application/json"}
UPSTREAM RESPONSE: 302 Found
Headers: {Location: "https://sso.company/login", Content-Type: "text/html; charset=utf-8"}
BODY: <!DOCTYPE html>...
```

anna.d: Thanks. Two things to surface to customer: 1) this is an upstream auth redirect — temporary and will be fixed by renewing the token or ensuring their token isn't intermittently expiring; 2) workaround: set mode to non-strict or add a retry that checks status code before attempting to parse.

cheng.w: From eng side: I'll open ENG-RUNTIME ticket to add defensive behavior — if response content-type != application/json or status >= 400, return a structured error object instead of raw parse error, so SDKs can surface a nicer message. Also will add metrics to track % of non-JSON responses during structured mode.

lauren.k: In the short term, support should ask customer to: 1) confirm token scope/expiry; 2) retry with explicit header --header 'Accept: application/json' (they already set it but we saw some samples where proxy stripped it); 3) if they can, include x-request-id from their failing call so we can trace a sample.

mike.s: Customer provided one failing request-id: r-3497. I attached logs to the ticket.

support-bot: Created escalation ENG-RUNTIME-432 and linked ticket ACME-812 -> ENG-RUNTIME-432 :rotating_light:

anna.d: Proposed reply to customer (short): 

anna.d: "Thanks — we're investigating. Workarounds: 1) retry the call; 2) temporarily set mode to non-strict or add pre-check for HTTP status before parsing; 3) ensure token is not expiring and Accept header is set. We've opened an internal engineering ticket (ENG-RUNTIME-432) and will follow up."

mike.s: Sent that. Customer applied non-strict mode and error rate dropped to zero. They want ETA on a permanent fix.

cheng.w: I expect a patch for more graceful handling and better logging in edge by EOD tomorrow. Will update ENG ticket with repro and a small unit test reproducing the 302->html case.

lauren.k: Sounds good — assign to runtime oncall and include the failing request-ids. I'll tag infra to check if any recent proxy rules may drop Accept.

mike.s: Closing loop here for now, keeping the thread open until eng confirms. :thumbsup:
